**Use the table for questions 1–2.** Cinema, Saturday evening showing (one showing per screen). *Occupancy = % of seats sold.*

| Screen type | Screens | Seats per screen | Occupancy | Ticket price (€) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | 20 | 150 | 45% | 9 |
| Large format | 4 | 300 | 70% | 16 |
| VIP | 6 | 40 | 60% | 22 |

chart.title: Active users of a fitness app (thousands)

questions.stem: What percentage of the cinema's ticket revenue for the showing comes from VIP screens?
If occupancy on Standard screens rose from 45% to 54%, by what percentage would Standard ticket revenue rise?
questions.explain: 54/45 = 1.20 → +20%. 9 is the change in percentage points.

questions.stem: A hotel charges €110 per night for the first 3 nights and €90 per night for each further night, plus a tourist tax of €2.50 per person per night. What do two people pay for a 5-night stay in one room?
questions.explain: 330 + 180 = €510 + 2.50 × 2 × 5 = €25 → €535. €522.50 charges the tax per room; €575 charges every night at 110.

questions.stem: What number comes next? 1, 2, 4, 7, 11, 16, ?
In June, what percentage of the app's active users were paid users?
questions.explain: 39/(300 + 39) = 11.5%. 13% divides by free users only (wrong denominator).

questions.stem: Each paid user pays €8 a month. What was the total paid-subscription revenue from January to June?
questions.explain: Paid users summed: 20 + 22 + 26 + 30 + 35 + 39 = 172k × 8 = €1.376m. €312k is June only.

questions.stem: Between which two consecutive months did the number of paid users grow by the largest percentage?
questions.explain: +10.0%, +18.2%, +15.4%, +16.7%, +11.4%. April–May has the largest absolute rise (+5), not the largest percentage rise.

questions.stem: A nursery must have at least 1 adult for every 4 children under 2, and at least 1 adult for every 8 children aged 2 to 5. Each age group is supervised separately. There are 14 children under 2 and 27 children aged 2 to 5. What is the minimum number of adults needed?
questions.explain: 14/4 = 3.5 → 4 adults; 27/8 = 3.4 → 4 adults. Total 8. 7 pools the two groups; 6 rounds down.

questions.stem: Each row follows the same rule. Row 1: 4, 5, 14. Row 2: 7, 3, 13. Row 3: 6, 8, ?
A consultant bills €1,480 a day, for 21 days a month, over 10.5 months a year. Which is the best estimate of her annual billings?
A product sells for €25 and costs €13 per unit to make. Fixed costs are €18,000 a month. How many units must be sold each month to break even?
questions.explain: Margin per unit €12 → 18,000/12 = 1,500. 720 divides by the price.

questions.stem: A town's population of 250,000 grows by 4% a year. What will it be after 3 years, to the nearest thousand?
questions.explain: 250,000 × 1.04³ = 281,216. 280,000 adds 3 × 4% without compounding.

two.md: **Questions 13–14.** For each pair of statements, choose the option that best describes their relationship.

questions.stem:
All trains on the coastal line stop at Gandia. Some trains that stop at Gandia are express trains.

**Conclusion:** Some trains on the coastal line are express trains.
questions.explain: The express trains that stop at Gandia may belong to other lines.

questions.stem:
No full-time employees are paid by the hour. Some contractors are paid by the hour.

**Conclusion:** Some contractors are not full-time employees.
questions.explain: Contractors paid by the hour cannot be full-time employees.

questions.stem:
All projects approved by the board have a sponsor. Some projects with a sponsor are delayed. No delayed project receives extra funding.

Which statement must be true?
options: No board-approved project receives extra funding.
All projects with a sponsor were approved by the board.
Some projects with a sponsor do not receive extra funding.
Some delayed projects were approved by the board.
questions.explain: Sponsored projects that are delayed get no extra funding. A and E cannot be deduced; C reverses the premise.

questions.stem:
Whenever server load exceeds 90%, an automatic alert is sent to the IT team. No alert was sent on Tuesday.

Which statement must be true?
options: The IT team was not working on Tuesday.
Server load stayed below 50% on Tuesday.
Every alert means the load exceeded 90%.
Server load did not exceed 90% on Tuesday.
questions.explain: Contrapositive. C reverses the rule (alerts could be sent for other reasons).

questions.stem:
Five shops (Bakery, Chemist, Florist, Grocer, Newsagent) stand side by side in positions 1 to 5.
- The Florist is immediately to the right of the Bakery (one position higher).
- The Chemist is not at either end.
- The Grocer is to the left of the Newsagent.
- The Grocer is not next to the Bakery.
- The Newsagent is not in position 5.

Which shop is in position 4?
questions.explain: Testing the Bakery–Florist pair, only 4–5 leaves room for the rest. Grocer 1 and Chemist/Newsagent in 2–3 (two possible orders), but Bakery is always 4.

questions.stem:
Five speakers (Ruiz, Sol, Tomás, Uri, Vera) present in slots 1 to 5.
- Sol presents third.
- Vera presents before Ruiz.
- Uri presents immediately after Tomás.
- Ruiz does not present last.

Who presents last?
questions.explain: If Tomás–Uri were 1–2, Ruiz would end up last. So Vera, Ruiz, Sol, Tomás, Uri.

questions.stem:
Five products (K, L, M, N, O) are ranked 1st to 5th by sales, with no ties.
- K sold more than L.
- M sold more than K.
- N sold the least.
- O is not ranked 1st.

Which statement must be true?
questions.explain: Neither K nor L can be 1st (M is ahead of them), nor can O: 1st is M. The rest allows several orders.

questions.stem:
"We will hire 10 more call-centre agents, so customers' waiting times will fall by half."

Which assumption does the argument rely on?
options: The new agents will handle calls about as efficiently as current agents, and call volumes will not rise significantly.
The call centre will move to a new building.
The new agents will be cheaper than current ones.
Current agents are paid too little.
Customers prefer phone support to email.
questions.explain: More agents only cut waiting times if they perform as well and demand doesn't grow.

questions.stem:
"Restaurants that display calorie counts on their menus sell fewer high-calorie dishes. Displaying calorie counts makes customers choose healthier food."

Which statement, if true, most weakens the argument?
options: Restaurants that chose to display calorie counts had already removed most high-calorie dishes from their menus.
Healthy dishes are often more expensive.
Calorie counts are required by law in some countries.
Calorie counts are printed in small type.
questions.explain: They sell fewer high-calorie dishes because they offer fewer, not because of the labels.

questions.stem:
"Everyone I know who drinks green tea every day is healthy. Green tea clearly makes people healthy."

Which statement best describes the flaw in the argument?
options: It attacks people who don't drink tea.
It generalises from a small, unrepresentative group and treats an association as a cause.
It confuses green tea with other teas.
It relies on an expert's opinion.
It assumes green tea is expensive.
questions.explain: A small, unrepresentative sample, and correlation taken as cause (tea drinkers may lead healthier lives).

questions.stem:
A committee of 5 people is chosen from 4 engineers and 4 lawyers. It must include at least 2 engineers and at least 2 lawyers.

Which statement must be true?
options: The committee has more engineers than lawyers.
questions.explain: With 5 seats and at least 2 of each: 3 + 2 or 2 + 3.

questions.stem:
An office has 3 meeting rooms. On Monday, 8 one-hour meetings were held between 9:00 and 12:00, each starting on the hour and each in its own room.

Which statement must be true?
options: Every room was in use for all three hours.
Exactly one room was empty at 9:00.
One of the meetings lasted two hours.
One room was empty for two hours.
In at least two of the three hours, all three rooms were in use.
questions.explain: There are 9 slots (3 rooms × 3 hours) and 8 were used: only one is free, so at least two hours were fully booked.

questions.stem:
(1) A commercial bank raised its mortgage interest rates.
(2) The central bank raised its official interest rate the week before.
options: Statement 1 is the cause and statement 2 is its effect.
Statement 2 is the cause and statement 1 is its effect.
Both statements are effects of a common cause.
Both statements are effects of independent causes.
questions.explain: The central bank's rise (2) is passed on to mortgages (1).

questions.stem:
(1) Sales of winter coats rose sharply this year.
(2) Household heating bills rose sharply this year.
options: Statement 1 is the cause and statement 2 is its effect.
Statement 2 is the cause and statement 1 is its effect.
Both statements are effects of a common cause.
Both statements are effects of independent causes.
questions.explain: Effects of a common cause, such as a very cold winter.

questions.stem:
Sick-leave policy: employees must tell their manager before 10:00 on the first day of absence. Absences of more than 3 consecutive days require a doctor's note. Absences that are not reported are unpaid.

An employee told her manager at 9:15 and was absent for 4 consecutive days without a doctor's note. Which statement is correct?
options: She complied, because she reported the absence in time.
She did not comply, because she reported the absence too late.
Her absence is unpaid because it lasted 4 days.
She did not comply, because a doctor's note was needed.
questions.explain: She reported in time, but 4 days > 3 requires a doctor's note. The absence isn't unpaid: she did report it.

questions.stem:
Shipping rules: standard shipping costs €5, but is free on orders over €50. For deliveries to the islands, standard shipping is free only on orders over €100. Express delivery always costs €8 on top of any standard shipping charge.

A customer in Mallorca (an island) places a €75 order with express delivery. How much does she pay for shipping?
questions.explain: On the islands, €75 is not over €100 → €5 standard shipping + €8 express = €13. €8 applies the mainland rule.

questions.stem: Which statements can be concluded from the chart? **Select all that apply.**
options: Park B's visitors rose every year.
Park C was the most visited park in every year.
Total visitors to the three parks rose every year.
Park A's visitors fell every year.
Park B will overtake Park C by 2027.

questions.stem:
Delivery fleet, daily figures:

| Vehicle | Number | Km per vehicle per day | Fuel use (litres per 100 km) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Van | 12 | 150 | 9 |
| Truck | 4 | 220 | 25 |
| Car | 6 | 90 | 6 |

Which statements can be concluded from the data? **Select all that apply.**
options: The trucks use more fuel per day in total than the vans.
The vans cover the most kilometres per day in total.
Total daily fuel use is under 400 litres.
The cars account for less than 10% of total daily fuel use.
Trucks are the least efficient choice for every delivery.
questions.explain: Litres/day: vans 162, trucks 220, cars 32.4 → total 414.4. A ✔. B ✔ 1,800 km vs 880 and 540. C ✗. D ✔ 7.8%. E ✗ cannot be concluded.

questions.stem: What happened to the Marketing budget between 2024 and 2025?
options: It cannot be determined from the data.
questions.explain: 0.30 × 2.0 = €0.60m and 0.24 × 2.5 = €0.60m. The share falls, the amount doesn't.

questions.stem:
Customers by age group and channel:

| Age group | Online | Store |
|---|---|---|
| 18–34 | 360 | 140 |
| 35–54 | 220 | 280 |
| 55+ | 70 | 330 |

What percentage of store customers are aged 55 or over?
questions.explain: Store customers = 750 → 330/750 = 44%. 82.5% is the store share among the over-55s.

questions.stem: Class A has 20 students with a mean score of 70. Class B has 30 students with a mean score of 80. What is the mean score of all 50 students?
questions.explain: (1,400 + 2,400)/50 = 76. 75 is the simple average.

questions.stem: A dataset contains 4, 8, 8, 10 and 15. The value 15 is corrected to 50. Which measures change?
options: The mean and the range only
questions.explain: Mean 9 → 16 and range 11 → 46. Median (8) and mode (8) don't change.

questions.stem: A product sold 200 units in January and 250 in February, then 200 again in March. Which statement is correct?
Two versions of a survey are combined. In version 1, a score of 1 means "strongly agree"; in version 2, 1 means "strongly disagree". What should you do before combining them?
options: Report the two versions as one without changes.
Average all scores as they are.
Recode one version so both use the same direction, then combine.
Use the median instead of the mean.
questions.explain: Reversed scales: recode before combining.

questions.stem: In a sales file, stores that did not send their figures are recorded with sales of 0. What is the problem, and what should you do?
options: Delete the stores from the company.
Replace the zeros with the highest store's sales.
Multiply all sales by the share of stores that reported.
The zeros understate totals and averages; mark these values as missing and follow up with the stores.
questions.explain: A 0 is not the same as "no data".

questions.stem: In an employee table, two different employees share the same ID number. What is the best fix?
options: Ignore it if it happens rarely.
Assign unique IDs and make the ID field enforce uniqueness.
questions.explain: The key must be unique; fix it and prevent repeats.

questions.stem: You want to show how the 2025 budget is split between four departments. Which chart is most appropriate?
options: Line chart of each department over ten years
questions.explain: Parts of a whole at one point in time with few categories → pie (or a single 100% bar).

questions.stem: A company's sales fell steadily for five years. A presentation shows a chart of only the last three months, during which sales rose slightly, under the title "Sales are growing". What is the problem?
options: The chart should be a pie chart.
The chart has too few colours.
The time window was chosen selectively and hides the long-term decline.
questions.explain: A cherry-picked time window.
